newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five dead in Colombian jail riot.
newsitem.headline: Five dead in Colombian jail riot.

text.p: Inmates killed at least five prison guards and took 15 hostages in a riot at a jail in northern Colombia on Thursday evening, prison authorities said.

The prisoners are armed and in control of the jail compound, officials said. At least five of the prison's 500 inmates were injured in a shoot-out during which they managed to rob the guards of their pistols and night sticks.
Police and army surrounded the prison in Valledupar, in Cesar province, and fired bullets and tear-gas over the walls.

"A prisoner has reported that five guards are dead and they are holding 15 hostages. The inmates have seized the guards weapons and the situation is still not under control," a spokeswoman of the National Prisons' Institute INPEC said. The deputy prison director, guards and administrative staff, were among the hostages, the spokeswoman said.

"The dead and injured are inside the jail and the problems are still continuing. The shooting has died down but the inmates have taken over the jail," a police spokesman told Reuters by phone from Valledupar.

The prisoners, among whom are a number of convicted leftist guerrillas, called for doctors, Red Cross officials and the local human rights' ombudsman to go to the jail to negotiate an end to the riot. Their demands include an end to overcrowding and better health conditions, the prison spokeswoman said.
